text:
sam: Raising a concern from runtime: probe-driven route suggestions are noisy and some tenants are burning lots of probes that destabilize routing. We need a design for probe budgets and throttles.

leo: Agreed. We currently accept any runtime suggestion if it passes proof checks, but no rate limiting. Tenants doing A/B style traffic shaping can cause oscillation.

mina: Proposal: per-tenant probe budget (tokens/sec) enforced at runtime. Each probe suggestion consumes N tokens based on scope: lightweight check=1, full latency sweep=5, heavyweight fairness eval=20. Budgets refill at a configurable rate, with a small burst allowance.

kate: How do budgets interact with SLA-critical tenants? We may want higher budgets for enterprise accounts under Dedicated. Also we need a global safety cap.

sam: Right. Add a tiering model: free tier default budget 5 tps, standard 20 tps, enterprise 200 tps. Budgets are applied per-tenant per-region. Global cap ensures noisy tenants can't exhaust cluster probes.

leo: Enforcement point: runtime should decrement tokens atomically when emitting probe request. If budget exhausted, runtime returns advisory_rejected with reason=budget_exhausted and optionally queue the probe subject to backoff.

mina: Backoff semantics: exponential backoff with jitter. After a probe is rejected runtime can schedule a lightweight sampling probe at a low rate (e.g., 0.1 tps) to keep telemetry warm. Also emit metric tenant.probe.backoff.count.

kate: Billing note: we could surface budget usage to billing dashboard and charge for overage or require increased commitments for higher budgets. For now, start with soft limits and visibility.

sam: How to charge different costs for different probe types? We need a cost-weight mapping in the policy artifact or tenant config. Example mapping: {"light":1,"medium":5,"heavy":20}. Keep mapping mutable by ops.

leo: We also need quota safety for rollouts: during canaries, we should preserve a fraction of the tenant's budget reserved for control-plane sanity checks (e.g., 10% reserved). Prevents canary probes from starving production checks.

mina: Implementation detail: runtime maintains token-bucket per tenant keyed by (tenant_id, region, tier). Token refill is periodic and persisted in memory only; safe to lose on restart because budgets are soft. For stronger guarantees, we can persist a small leaky counter in the control plane.

kate: Observation/tracing: every accepted or rejected probe must emit a compact event: tenant, probe_type, tokens_consumed, remaining_tokens, decision, proof_fingerprint. This ties into policy-service audit logs.

sam: Policy engine interactions: when an advisory arrives, policy-service should check proof correctness and also check budget state if the service owns enforcement. Which side enforces? Runtime is closest to action, but policy-service could offer central quota for analytics and cross-runtime enforcement.

leo: Hybrid approach: runtime enforces fast-path local budget; policy-service maintains a soft global view and emits alerts when divergence occurs. Also policy-service can take enforcement over persistent mode for enterprise (where we want stronger guarantees).

mina: Edge cases: duplicate probes due to retries; token decrement must be idempotent for retried probe_uuid. Runtimes should accept a probe_uuid and reject double-charges if seen recently. Store a small cache of recent probe_uuids per tenant (ttl short).

kate: Security: tenant-supplied probe payloads must be size-limited to avoid DoS; we should reject oversized probe requests before budget check.

sam: Monitoring: dashboards: tenant.probe.tokens.remaining, tenant.probe.reject.rate, tenant.probe.accept.latency, tenant.probe.backoff.count. Add alerts for sustained reject.rate > 1% for top 100 tenants.

leo: Policy authoring UX: add optional "probe_budget_hint" in compiled artifact so policies can suggest token weights for probe types. Runtime still enforces global tenant quotas.

mina: Default probe weight table suggestion: light=1, medium=5, heavy=20, re-evalable per tenant. Include example artifact snippet in RFC.

kate: Rollout plan: implement runtime local enforcement behind a feature flag, roll canary 5% tenants, monitor metrics for false positives. Then enable policy-service soft view and alerts. Only after 2 weeks of stable signals flip flag for all.

ops-bot: deploy:runtime-probe-quota v0.1 -> canary (5%) :white_check_mark: <https://ci/redwood/900001>

sam: Action items:
- mina: draft RFC describing budget model, probe types, idempotency, and metrics.
- leo: prototype runtime token-bucket and recent-probe cache.
- kate: work with billing on visibility and tiers.
- sam: add arch-checklist and monitoring dashboards.

mina: I'll include two example scenarios in the RFC: (1) a spike from A/B testing tenant causing rejections and graceful backoff, (2) enterprise tenant with high budget and reserved canary slice.

leo: One more tradeoff: strict quotas reduce probe-driven optimization velocity. We should keep default behavior permissive with strong observability and only hard-limit after confirmed abuse. Document that in RFC.

mina: Filing RFC WIP to docs/rfcs and will ping arch-review. Thanks.
